findings.message: The redirect strip covers `N>&M` and redirects to /dev/null. It does not cover the bash `&>file` and `&>>file` forms, or a redirect to a real file written with `&>`. The `&` in `&>` is still treated as a command separator, so the leftover fragment (`>/tmp/c.log`) matches nothing in ALLOWED. Strip `&>>?\s*\S+` before splitting, add the same `&>` form for /dev/null, and add rows to the test table.
findings.scenario: Block mode, subagent at its cap runs `git commit -m x &>/tmp/c.log`. The `&>` is not stripped, so the split yields the parts `git commit -m ''  x` and `>/tmp/c.log`. The second part fails ALLOWED, so committing() returns False and the commit is denied with exit 2. That is the same good-faith-commit denial the previous round reported for `2>&1`.

findings.message: The pipe fix allows only `head` and `tail` as extra commands. Other read-only filters on the same pipeline (`wc`, `grep`, `cat`, `sort`) are still denied in block mode, so the fix covers the named example and not the class. Either decide on a deliberate filter list and test it, or document that only head and tail are accepted.
findings.scenario: Block mode, `git diff --stat | wc -l` or `git log --oneline | grep fix`: the second part is not in ALLOWED, so the whole command is denied with exit 2. `git log | head -5` passes.
